newsitem.title: USA: ADM Q2 below estimates, outlook favorable.
newsitem.headline: ADM Q2 below estimates, outlook favorable.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co reported lower than expected fiscal second quarter earnings, but the outlook for its results is favorable due to lower grain costs.
"Basically I think this quarter was disappointing, but it still looks favorable for the year," Dain Bosworth analyst Bonnie Wittenburg said.
One uncertainty going forward is ADM's pricing for high fructose corn syrup, a sweetener that is used in foods and beverages, according to analysts who were on an ADM conference call.
Analysts said ADM is currently negotiating its high fructose corn syrup pricing.

"It is very clear that they're expecting some pressure on high fructose corn syrup pricing," Merrill Lynch analyst Leonard Teitelbaum said. "However, we're looking for volumes to pick up, about six percent for the year" for both the industry and ADM.
Earlier today, ADM reported net earnings for the second quarter ended December 31 were $0.35 a share, down from $0.41 a year ago.
Analysts said earnings were below estimates. According to First Call, the consensus was for a flat quarter.
On an operating basis, excluding all LIFO inventory adjustments and other items, ADM earned $0.26 a share in the second quarter, down from $0.40 a year ago, analysts said.
Analysts said the agribusiness giant's earnings were hurt by remaining inventories of high-priced corn.
"They still had some high-priced grain," Wittenburg said. "This issue is mostly behind them."
ADM shares traded off 5/8 at 21-7/8, after hitting an intra-day low earlier of 21-1/4.
